title: How to Thrive as a Single Christian
excerpt: Singleness is not a waiting room. The church has often treated it that way, and single people have often believed it. Both were wrong.
body:
Somewhere along the way the church started talking about singleness as a problem to be solved, a temporary condition you endure until the real life starts. I have done this myself, from a pulpit, without meaning to, by the way I prayed for single people and the way I never quite let them lead anything that married couples led. We made a whole stage of life sound like a holding pattern. Then we wondered why single Christians felt like they were sitting in the back of the room.

Paul did not think this way. He was single, and he wrote that he wished more people were free to live as he did (1 Corinthians 7:7). Jesus was single. The two people the New Testament holds up most are not married. That should at least slow us down before we treat marriage as the goal and singleness as the detour.

## Stop living provisionally

The deepest trap of singleness is the provisional life. You do not buy the good furniture because you might move when you marry. You do not put down roots in a church because you might meet someone in another city. You hold your whole life loosely, waiting for the second half to begin, and meanwhile the only half you have been given slips by unlived.

The correction is not denial. It is commitment. Plant something. Buy the dishes. Join the church and serve in it like you will be there in ten years, because you might. A life held provisionally is a life half-refused, and God did not give you a provisional life. He gave you this one.

## Build a household that is not romantic

We have shrunk the word family until it means only spouse and children. The Bible's word for the people you do life with is bigger than that. The early church called each other brother and sister and meant it, sharing meals and money and burdens.

Singleness goes wrong when it becomes isolation. It goes well when it becomes a different shape of belonging. Make a standing dinner. Take a family in your church and become a fixture in their kids' lives. Travel with friends. Be the one who shows up. Loneliness is not cured by marriage and it is not cured by being alone with your thoughts. It is cured by being woven into people who count on you.

## Use the freedom you actually have

Paul's argument for singleness was not that it hurts less. It was that it frees you for undivided devotion (1 Corinthians 7:32-35). A married person's time and money and attention are rightly divided. Yours are not, and that is not a deprivation. It is a capacity.

You can say yes to the mission trip. You can give more than the median because you do not have a mortgage built for two incomes and three children. You can sit with the dying friend until two in the morning. The freedom is real, and the question is whether you will spend it on the kingdom or on yourself. Most of us spend it on ourselves. That is the actual temptation of singleness, and almost no one names it.

## Let the longing be honest

None of this means the desire for marriage is wrong, and I am not going to tell you to pray it away. You can want a thing God has not given and still live fully. The two are not in competition. Hannah wept in the temple and was not rebuked for it (1 Samuel 1). The longing is allowed to be real. What it is not allowed to do is run your life from the shadows, turning every gathering into a search and every friendship into a disappointment that it was not more.

Name the longing to God plainly. Then set it down and go live. The longing will still be there tomorrow. So will the life you are refusing to live while you wait.

## This week

Do one thing that a provisional life would not do. Buy something for your home you have been deferring until marriage. Or commit to a role in your church that assumes you will be there in three years. Pick the one that exposes how much you have been waiting, and do it on purpose.

Singleness is not less. It was the soil the church grew in. The question is not when your real life begins. It already has.
